citations.assessment: The Shilat entry discusses divergent traditions on Shilat’s identity and the attribution of the Haman genealogy.

Sanhedrin explicitly reports descendants of Haman who studied Torah in Bnei Brak. This digital Bavli witness does not name Shmuel; the named identification is recorded in the Shilat entry and the mystical source discussed below.
Bava Batra has the garden, the thirteen years, Rav’s question, and the teacher’s reply.
The report of the royal agent appears in the cited chapter of Ketubot.
Eruvin supplies the linked Rav Yehudah–Shmuel bar Shilat–Rav attribution.
Sukkah expressly identifies Rav Yehudah as Shmuel bar Shilat’s son and reports Rav’s ruling.
Rav’s instruction regarding his eulogy is exact. The witness writes Shilat where Heilprin has Shila.
Sukkah identifies the same Rav Yehudah as his son.
Judges gives Shamgar, the six hundred Philistines and the ox-goad. The mystical identification is separately cited.
Rav’s directions give age six and feeding like an ox. The Bavli then restricts corrective blows to a sandal strap; the mystical work’s use of the ox-goad is its own interpretation.
Heilprin gives these words in a different order from the Hebrew of Judges 5:20. The verse’s order of the three words yields the initials of Haman.
Daniel is the verse expounded in Bava Batra.
The Bavli directly applies the verse to teachers and names Shmuel as its example. The Haman and Sisera interpretation is Heilprin’s application of the mystical tradition.
The named text identifies Shamgar with Shmuel bar Shilat and continues with the teacher pun, the six orders, and the ox-goad interpretation.
The parallel in the Ari corpus expressly links Shmuel to the root of Kayin, names Haman and Sisera, and gives the biblical words in their acrostic order.

notes.text: The checked Sanhedrin says descendants of Haman studied in Bnei Brak. The identification with Shmuel bar Shilat belongs to a separate textual and interpretive tradition.
In Judges 5:20 the words are הכוכבים ממסלותם נלחמו. Their initials spell המן. Heilprin quotes הכוכבים נלחמו ממסילותם and attributes the acrostic to the cited mystical tradition.
